$comment: Curation on Kraft is community-driven: any member can shelve a list and write why (brand canon). Nine are named and appear in the product; the rest exist as a count only. Each curator has a beat — this is what makes playlist attribution feel real rather than decorative.

curators.name: Sofía Reyes
curators.bio: Ran a record shop for eleven years before Kraft. Believes a playlist should end somewhere different from where it started.

curators.name: Adé Mensah
curators.bio: Crate-digs in Accra and Lagos. Writes the liner notes nobody asked for and everybody reads.

curators.name: Ingrid Halvorsen
curators.bio: Former concert-hall programmer. Sequences ambient records the way other people sequence arguments.

curators.name: Marcus Pike
curators.bio: Forty years of Blue Note pressings in a spare room. Has opinions about run-out grooves.

curators.name: Haruka Nakagawa
curators.bio: Writes about records the way people write about weather — constantly, and with feeling.

curators.name: Théo Marchand
curators.bio: Twelve years behind a booth. Now argues that a good playlist is just a set with the applause taken out.

curators.name: Nadia Ilić
curators.bio: Fanzine editor turned curator. Sequences for tension, not for comfort.

curators.name: Luana Andrade
curators.bio: Grew up in her father's rehearsal room. Can tell a Rio pressing from a Bogotá one by the hiss.

curators.name: Amara Diallo
curators.bio: Started on pirate radio at sixteen. Still sequences like she is filling a two-hour slot.

$note: totalCurators is brand canon (see CANON.md): members with at least one list on the shelf. The nine named above are the ones with a byline in the product; the rest exist only as a count. Nobody is paid to curate and the product never says otherwise.
